title: Lesson 1: Noticing and Wondering: What Happens during the Day and Night?
objective: Students will listen to and discuss texts and videos about daytime and nighttime activities to ask and answer questions and describe observations about what happens during the day and night.

what_is_taught.skill: answer questions about a text using details
describe activities of animals and people during day and night
use imagination to understand figurative language about the sun and moon
sort pictures into categories based on attributes
use sentence frames to describe observations
participate in partner discussions using protocols
reflect on personal experiences related to daytime and nighttime
use vocabulary words related to writing and categorization

student_actions.recognition_identification: listen and identify details in read-alouds and videos
student_actions.oral_production: answer questions orally, share observations, explain sorting categories, participate in partner talk
student_actions.matching_sorting_sequencing: sort picture cards into daytime and nighttime categories
student_actions.procedural_application: use sorting and partner discussion protocols
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain why pictures belong in categories and provide evidence from texts and videos
student_actions.comprehension_response: answer questions about texts and videos, describe observations about day and night activities, reflect on personal experiences related to day and night activities, use sentence frames to communicate ideas orally, paraphrase story content, act or sketch story activities for comprehension support if needed, mime observations to communicate ideas for ELLs, compare and contrast observations with personal experiences, respond to total participation technique prompts, share thinking with partners and whole group

evidence.quote: 'What are some things that Elvin wondered about?' (if the sun and moon had stories; if the sun and moon danced and had songs)
'What are some things that Elvin shared with us because he wondered about the sun, moon, and stars?' (photographs, songs, movement routines, books)

'What does a writer do? Why do you think Elvin is sharing his wonderings about the sun, moon, and stars with a writer?' (A writer tells stories and shares information. Elvin wonders if he can tell stories and write about the sun, moon, and stars.)
'What, in the story, makes you think so?' (Responses will vary.)
'What is Elvin wondering about now?' (if he can write about the sun and moon)
I can ask and answer questions about day and night based on the text What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees.
'What do you think the author means when she writes 'what the sun sees' and 'what the moon sees'?' (Responses will vary.)
'When the author wrote about what the sun sees, was she writing about daytime or nighttime?' (daytime)
'What did the sun 'see' animals and people doing during the daytime?' (busy children, crowded streets, animals in the barn)
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
'When the author wrote about what the moon sees, was she writing about daytime or nighttime?' (nighttime)
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Tell students that now they will sort pictures and words of activities that might happen during the day or during nighttime.
Invite students to begin the Sorting protocol.
'What does it mean to sort pictures into different categories?' (We will put pictures that go together in one group or category and other pictures that go together in another group or category.)
'Can you explain what is the same about the pictures in this categories?' (Responses will vary.)
'What are you sorting into the daytime category? Why?' (Responses will vary.)
'What are you sorting into the nighttime category? Why?' (Responses will vary.)
After 7-8 minutes, refocus students and invite one or two pairs to share what they sorted into the daytime category and what they sorted into the nighttime category.
"What is something you did that helped you succeed in the Sorting protocol? I'll give you time to think and discuss with a partner.' (Responses will vary.)
I can describe what animals and people do during the day and night based on observations of pictures and videos.

'What are some activities that people might do during the day when the sun is out? What are some activities that people might do during the night when the moon is out?' (During the day, people might play, walk outside, and go to school. During the night, people might watch television at home, take a bath, and go to bed.)

Tell students that as they watch the videos, they should look carefully to see what they notice and observe about the sky, the sun, the moon, and what animals and people are doing during the daytime and during the nighttime. Tell students they should also think about the questions they have as they watch the videos.
Guide students through the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol using this question:
Provide a sentence frame if necessary:
As students share, circulate and continue to use the Speaking and Listening Checklist to assess their progress toward the learning target.
Refocus students whole group and play 'Downtown Boston at Night.'
Repeat the process above for the protocol, using the following question and sentence stem:
Refocus students whole group and invite a few volunteers to share out to the whole group.
Invite students to turn and talk:
Circulate and listen as students share out. Select two or three students to share their responses with the whole group.

Offer students specific, positive feedback on their work during the lesson to answer questions about daytime and nighttime. (Example: 'Haiyan related what she saw in the video clip during the night to her father because he goes to work at night; RaShawn noticed that during the day, there are a lot more people, but at night there were a lot more animals.')

For ELLs: Share successful communication as well as one or two common, important language errors. For example, if students made errors with verb tense, discuss an example and guide the students to correct it. Example: 'Some of you were saying, 'I noticed that during the night, people and animals sleeping.' We need to add one more word before sleeping so that this is a complete sentence. What are the people and animals doing?'

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model fluent, expressive read-alouds of texts about the sun, moon, and stars; model use of sorting and partner discussion protocols; model use of sentence frames for describing observations; provide positive feedback and language correction during closing.

scope.breadth: multiple texts and media about day and night activities
scope.depth: understanding and describing daytime and nighttime activities, sorting and categorizing, using language to explain and reflect

sections_covered.warm_up: Reading Aloud: 'Elvin, the Boy Who Loved the Sky,' Part 6
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Reading Aloud: What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees
sections_covered.guided_practice: Sorting Protocol: Daytime and Nighttime Activities; Video and Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face: What Happens during the Day and Night?
sections_covered.check_for_understanding: Throughout lesson via total participation techniques and partner sharing
sections_covered.differentiated_reinforce: Sentence frames and acting/sketching for ELLs
sections_covered.differentiated_extend: Encouraging students to compare and contrast video observations with personal experiences

supports.english_language_learners: Provides visual text display, sentence frames, acting/sketching, miming, and language correction to support comprehension and oral production.
supports.universal_design_udl: Uses multiple modalities including read-alouds, videos, partner talk, sorting hands-on activity, and sentence frames to engage diverse learners.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Offers heavier comprehension support through acting or sketching story activities and sentence frames.
supports.above_level_extend: Invites students to compare and contrast observations with personal experiences and to explain reasoning for sorting categories.

assessment.method: Observations of student responses during read-aloud discussions, sorting protocol, partner talk, and whole group sharing.
assessment.recognition_vs_production: Both recognition of details in texts and videos and oral production of explanations and reflections.

text_complexity.quantitative: read-aloud mediation; quantitative measure not specified

text_complexity.reader_and_task: Read-aloud removes decoding demands; students engage in listening comprehension, partner discussions, and categorization tasks.
